questions.q: What does the book say makes someone a spark?
a: The way they act, not the title they hold
The size of the team they manage
The salary level they have reached
The years they have spent at the company
questions.why: The overview and Lesson 1 stress that leadership comes from behavior and can appear at any level.

questions.q: What is cognitive flexibility, as described in the summary?
a: Changing your usual thinking patterns to find new solutions
Sticking to a proven method no matter what
Ignoring problems until they resolve themselves
Making decisions quickly without reflection
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines it as altering typical thinking to solve a problem, like toasting bread in the oven when the toaster breaks.

a: Slowing your thinking and pausing before reacting
Trusting your first instinct every time
Avoiding all feedback from colleagues
Working longer hours than everyone else
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it means halting instinctive reactions to give a more effective response, especially to criticism.

questions.q: How does a spark respond when criticized at work?
a: By responding constructively and asking how to improve
By defending themselves and explaining the misunderstanding
By escalating the issue to a manager
By withdrawing from the team until things calm down
questions.why: Lesson 2 contrasts the defensive reaction most people have with the spark’s habit of asking for ways to improve.

questions.q: What does the summary say blame is, in evolutionary terms?
a: A survival mechanism we use when we feel threatened
A learned habit picked up in childhood
A sign of strong leadership potential
A modern invention of office culture
questions.why: Lesson 3 says diverting blame is a natural survival response to seeing something as a threat, which sparks resist.
